posts.text:
France has one official language. A government report in 1999 counted 75 others spoken on French soil.

Every colour on this map was somebody's mother tongue — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Most of the map is Romance, split three ways. North: the langues d'oïl — Picard, Norman, Champenois, Poitevin. South: Occitan, here broken into Gascon, Lengadocian, Auvergnat, Provençal. East: Arpitan, also called Franco-Provençal.

2/ Oïl and oc were once just the two words for "yes." Dante used the difference to classify Europe's Romance tongues. The line between them runs roughly across the middle of France and is still visible in place names and cooking fats.

3/ Find the small patch marked Francien, around Paris. That is standard French. It didn't win on merit — it won because the royal court, the courts of law and the printing presses were sitting on top of it.

4/ Four colours on this map aren't Romance at all. Breton is Celtic, carried across the Channel from Britain in late antiquity. Alsatian, Lothringish and Flemish are Germanic. And Basque, bottom left, is related to no known living language.

5/ The squeeze began early. The Ordinance of Villers-Cotterêts, 1539, required French rather than Latin — or anything else — in legal documents. Standardisation started as an administrative convenience, not a cultural programme.

6/ It became one in the Revolution. Abbé Grégoire's 1794 report treated regional speech as an obstacle to citizenship and called for its eradication. Then the Ferry laws of 1881-82 made primary school free, compulsory and monolingual.

7/ In many schools a pupil caught speaking Breton or Occitan was handed a token — le symbole — and had to pass it on by catching a classmate. Whoever held it at the end of the day was punished. Children were made the enforcers.

8/ It worked. Breton had roughly a million speakers around 1950 and is now usually estimated near 200,000. France signed the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages in 1999 and has never ratified it.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
